content:
Connor O'Brien: heads up for the next Private cut — we need release notes to explicitly call out backup/restore changes + upgrade caveats + compatibility notes. We got a few moving pieces landing (installer + helm charts + docs + metrics). Want to avoid "surprise" restores failing.

Sahana Iyer: +1. Can we enumerate what’s actually customer-visible vs internal? I’m trying to keep the notes crisp but we should include the scary parts (compat + required versions).

Elliot Price: docs PR is in (redwood-docs#812). It has a customer guide + DR checklist. But release notes need an explicit pointer + quick summary.

Kira Thompson: I can draft the release note section. Need inputs on:
- backup artifact format / versioning (is it stable now?)
- whether restores are supported cross-version
- any breaking changes around encryption (KMS envelope)

Ethan Park: from control-plane side:
- `backup create` and `restore apply` are now supported entrypoints in the private installer (redwood-private-installer#482, #489)
- backup format is manifest + encrypted payload; we added backup format versioning + compatibility checks on restore (redwood-private-installer#512)
- important: we do NOT back up secret material. we back up references/metadata, and restore expects same external secret backends to be available + access configured.

Marcus Lin: please make sure release notes say this plainly. We’ve had customers assume "backup includes secrets" and then get surprised.

Hanae Suzuki: encryption-wise: envelope encryption support added via provider interface (redwood-private-installer#505). Default is local DEK + wrapping key; for VPC installs, recommend customer-managed KMS where possible. Also: if KMS is down, backup creation fails hard (by design) — don’t want to silently write unencrypted artifacts.

Sean Gallagher: from SRE/runbooks: also call out observability pack changes: dashboards/alerts are new (observability-pack#94 + slo-toolkit#67). Might not be "breaking" but it’s worth mentioning for folks who rely on paging policies.

Connor O'Brien: ok, here’s what I think release notes MUST include (customer-facing):
1) New toolkit capability: supported backup/restore workflows for Redwood Private control plane.
2) Compatibility: backup artifacts have a format version; restores validate compatibility and may refuse with a clear error.
3) Upgrade caveat: restore tooling must match (or be within supported range of) the version that produced the backup.
4) What is / isn’t in the backup (esp secrets).
5) Required component versions (installer + chart values)

Sahana Iyer: can you be specific on version range? Like "same minor" or "same major"? If we can’t state it, we should at least say "see compatibility matrix" and link.

Ethan Park: current implementation: safe guidance is "same major" at minimum. We’ve tested N to N+1 minor for restore (within same major), but I’m not ready to claim cross-major. For the notes, I’d say:
- Supported: restore using the same Redwood Private platform version that created the backup.
- Best-effort: restore using a newer patch/minor in the same major, if compatibility check passes.
- Not supported: restore across major versions (unless explicitly stated in docs/compat matrix).

Kira Thompson: that works. I’ll phrase as "recommended" + "supported". Also include: "keep the installer binary used to create backups"? Customers in air-gapped might not be able to fetch older tooling.

Connor O'Brien: yes, add that to caveats for on-prem/air-gapped: keep the release bundle / installer artifacts alongside backups.

Hanae Suzuki: and mention KMS key rotation: restoring requires access to the wrapping key that encrypted the DEK. If they rotate/disable keys, restore will fail. We should push them to document their key lifecycle.

Marcus Lin: careful wording: we don’t want to sound like "don’t rotate keys". Say "ensure rotated keys remain decrypt-capable for retention period".

Sean Gallagher: also add the operational caveat: backups aren’t useful unless restore is tested. Point to the restore drill guidance + suggested cadence.

Elliot Price: on docs side we have a section "Testing restores / DR drills" and troubleshooting. I can add an anchor link for release notes to reference.

Sahana Iyer: can you drop a proposed release note snippet here so we can align before it goes into the release checklist?

Kira Thompson: draft (feel free to edit):

"Private: Backup/Restore + DR Readiness (Day-2 Ops)
- Added supported `backup create` and `restore apply` workflows for Redwood Private control plane state.
- Backup artifacts now include a versioned manifest and encrypted payload. Restore validates artifact compatibility and will refuse unsupported combinations.
- Upgrade/compatibility: Restores are supported using the same Redwood Private version that created the backup. Restoring with a newer patch/minor in the same major version may be supported if the compatibility check passes. Cross-major restores are not supported unless explicitly noted in the compatibility matrix.
- Security: Backups do not include secret material; they include references/metadata only. Restores require the same external secret backends and permissions to be present.
- Encryption: Envelope encryption is supported (customer-managed KMS where applicable). Ensure key lifecycle/rotation preserves decrypt capability for the backup retention period.
- Recommended: Perform periodic restore drills; see docs for validation checklist and observability signals." 

Connor O'Brien: this is good. Add one more bullet: "If using Helm charts, enable backup CronJob values/RBAC" and note chart version requirement (redwood-helm-charts#131 + #138).

Ethan Park: +1. Also mention there’s a new backup status endpoint surfaced for UI/automation (redwood#24318) if we’re including that in this cut.

Sahana Iyer: do we know if #24318 is definitely in the release? If it slips, we shouldn’t promise it.

Connor O'Brien: fair. I’ll gate that in the release notes as "if enabled" / "when available" OR omit for now. We can keep it out unless we confirm it’s in the tagged build.

Elliot Price: for doc link, use the docs page path once merged. For now: "See: Private → Backup & Restore Guide". I’ll comment back with the final URL when we publish.

Marcus Lin: quick security nit: ensure release notes don’t imply backups can be stored unencrypted on NFS/S3. We should say "encrypted at rest" and mention customer storage policies still apply.

Kira Thompson: updated snippet w/ helm + encryption line.

Sahana Iyer: 👍 I’ll add this to the release note template + tie it to the release checklist item in the Drive checklist doc. Connor, can you confirm final wording by EOD?

Connor O'Brien: yep. I’ll review + sign off. Also adding a checkbox in the release checklist: "Backup/restore compatibility + upgrade caveats included".

Sean Gallagher: thanks all. Once notes are in, I’ll make sure on-call runbook references the same caveats so support isn’t guessing.

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: closing the loop — Kira/Elliot, please ping when docs URL is final so we can update the release notes with a direct link.
